group.passage: Barbie is a 29-cm-tall plastic doll with the figure of an adult woman, introduced on March 9, 1959 by Mattel, Inc., a toy company in Southern California. Ruth Handler, who co-founded Mattel with her husband, presided over the doll’s presentation. Barbie’s appearance was modeled on the German Bild Lilli doll, a suggestive gag gift for men based upon a cartoon character from the West German newspaper Bild Zeitung. Since the doll’s debut, its body has sparked controversy. In a Mattel-sponsored market study before the doll’s official release, mothers criticized Barbie for having “too much of a figure.” However, to find a way around this issue, Mattel promoted Barbie directly to children through television after the doll was introduced to the market. In response to consumer demand, in 1961, Mattel introduced Barbie’s ultimate “accessory”— her boyfriend, Ken. In 1963, Mattel added Barbie’s best friend, Midge, and in 1964 her little sister Skipper. By 1968, Barbie had been given “friend” dolls of color, including Christie and Francie, but Barbie itself wasn’t released as an African American version until 1980. Since the 1970s, Barbie has been criticized for materialism and unrealistic body proportions. Still, many women who played with the doll consider Barbie an alternative to the restrictive gender roles of the 1950s. Unlike baby dolls that taught nursing back then, Barbie, equipped with career accessories, was a model for economic self-sufficiency. In fact, Barbie’s résumé included, among others, airline pilot, astronaut, physician, Olympic athlete, and U.S. presidential candidate, her first ever career being a teen model. Barbie, having no parents or offspring, was also not defined by relationships of responsibility to men or family. When consumers called for a Barbie-sized baby in the early 1960s, Mattel did not make Barbie a mother, but instead released “Barbie Baby-Sits” playset. There is no doubt that Barbie is a very popular collectible. Aficionados are interested in both vintage Barbies and the special edition Barbies that Mattel creates to cater to this market. Although Barbie’s sales aren’t as strong as in the 1990s, they still exceed one billion dollars annually with two Barbies sold every second.

questions.stem:
In what order did the following incidents happen?
a. Mattel sponsored a market study on consumer acceptance of Barbie.
b. The German Bild Lilli doll was created based on a cartoon character.
c. Barbie officially debuted as a creation of Mattel, Inc.’s Ruth Handler.
d. Mattel broadcast Barbie commercials directly to children through TV.
According to the passage, which of the following statements is true about Barbie?

options.A: The first Black Barbie was introduced in 1968 to meet the needs of consumers.
options.B: Barbie has been criticized for representing restrictive gender roles since the 1970s.
options.C: Barbie’s best friend and little sister were created within five years after her launch.
options.D: Barbie was welcomed by mothers because she taught positive family relationships.
